symbols.name: LiveCouncilRefused
symbols.note: Exception raised when live=True is required for real vendor adapters. Inherits RuntimeError.

symbols.name: live_egress_seats
symbols.note: Returns tuple of seat descriptions that could reach a real vendor. Uses shipped_classes, dispatch module, and _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS to determine liveness.

symbols.name: convene
symbols.note: Main council execution function. Partially shown; includes live-wire gate (if not live) and parameter documentation.

claims.text: A seat that can reach a real vendor was offered without ``live=True``.
claims.why: The docstring describes when the exception is raised, but the actual raise is not in this chunk; it likely appears later in convene.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT a ``ValueError``: every other refusal in :func:`convene` is a malformed-roster complaint, and "you were about to spend money" must be catchable on its own.
claims.why: The docstring compares to other refusals in convene, but those refusals are not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Name every seat that could actually reach a vendor.  FAIL-CLOSED.
claims.why: The function iterates participants and checks conditions to identify live seats; the logic defaults to assuming a seat is live unless proven otherwise (fail-closed).

claims.text: The question is not "is this class from :mod:`vendors`" -- it is "if ``ask()`` runs, does SHIPPED transport code execute".
claims.why: The function checks if the adapter is an instance of shipped_classes (classes from vendors module) and then checks if _dispatch is from _vendors module, and if hooks are original shipped transports.

claims.text: A seat is therefore counted as LIVE unless one of these is demonstrably true: * it is not one of the shipped concrete adapters at all ... * its ``_dispatch`` ... is defined OUTSIDE :mod:`daedalus.council.vendors` ... * its ``runner`` / ``chat`` hook is not one of :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS` ...
claims.why: The code implements exactly these three checks: isinstance check, dispatch module check, and hook substitution check.

claims.text: Everything else -- including an adapter shape this function has never seen -- is assumed able to spend money.
claims.why: If an adapter passes all checks (i.e., is a shipped class, dispatch from vendors, no hook substitution), it is appended to live list. Adapters that are not shipped classes are skipped (continue), so they are not considered live. But the doc says 'everything else' is assumed able to spend money; the code only adds to live if it passes all checks. This is consistent: non-shipped classes are skipped, so they are not in live list, meaning they are not considered live. The 'assumed able to spend money' applies to adapters that are shipped but have modified dispatch or hooks? Actually, the doc says 'everything else' meaning if none of the three conditions are true, the seat is live. That matches the code: if all checks pass, it's live.

claims.text: If :data:`_SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS` ever resolves empty (vendors renamed something), the hook test is SKIPPED rather than trivially satisfied, so the failure lands on the safe side.
claims.why: The code checks `if _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS:` before iterating hooks; if empty, the substituted flag remains False, so the adapter is not considered substituted, and thus remains live (since it passed earlier checks). This is safe because an empty list means no known transports, so any hook is assumed to be original? Actually, if empty, the check is skipped, so the adapter is not marked substituted, so it remains live. That is fail-closed (assuming live). The doc says 'the failure lands on the safe side' meaning if the list is empty, we assume the adapter is live (safer than assuming not live).

claims.text: ``participants`` are :class:`vendors.CouncilAdapter` instances -- read-only, tool-less, spawned outside the repo.  Every one of them is REQUESTED, and every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn per round even when it is missing: skipping an unavailable vendor would let a two-vendor council render identically to a four-vendor one.
claims.why: The docstring describes behavior of participants in the council execution, but the actual logic for handling missing vendors is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``trusted_vendors`` is the OPERATOR OPT-IN that lifts a vendor off the untrusted allow-list for this council only.  It is recorded per participant, because deciding OpenAI or Google is trusted with this repo's IP is a policy decision and a default argument must not make it.
claims.why: The docstring describes usage of trusted_vendors parameter, but the code that uses it is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``live`` is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False.  Any seat that still carries a shipped vendor transport (:func:`live_egress_seats`) raises :class:`LiveCouncilRefused` here -- before the council id, before the store, before the roster is chained, before one byte is dispatched.  Offline adapters (fakes, injected runners) are unaffected, so the replay harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: The docstring describes that LiveCouncilRefused is raised when live=False and live_egress_seats returns non-empty. The code in this chunk only shows `if not live:` but not the subsequent raise; the raise must be in the next chunk.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the live-wire gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach `sorted()` empty -- a council of nobody, chained as if it were real.
claims.why: The code before the comment does `participants = tuple(participants)`, which materializes the iterable into a tuple, preventing exhaustion.

observations.what: The chunk defines LiveCouncilRefused, live_egress_seats, and starts convene. The live-wire gate logic is only partially shown (if not live: is present, but the raise is missing).
The live_egress_seats function relies on _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS and _vendors which are not defined in this chunk. Their absence could cause runtime errors.

The docstring for live_egress_seats claims fail-closed behavior, but the logic may not cover all edge cases (e.g., if _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS is empty, the hook test is skipped, which might be too permissive).
